Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically unless you finish with SELECT <successful step> to choose an
already executed build. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Working procedure:
1. Record a compact visible-object inventory, including cropped foreground objects, and
   several approximate image landmarks across foreground, subject and background. Image
   coordinates estimated by eye are estimates, not measured calibration. Choose a coherent
   world scale; absolute size and camera distance are not identifiable from this image alone.
2. Parameterize camera pose, focal length and shift separately from object dimensions.
   Use room edge directions, verticals, visible top surfaces and depth-dependent size ratios
   to estimate viewpoint. Compare global framing against local silhouette disagreement.
   A focal change changes framing throughout the view; translation also changes parallax.
   Do not compensate for local shape errors by scaling the whole scene or camera together.
3. Build a complete economical scene first, with semantic Asset groups, explicit supports,
   major colors and distinctive outlines. Include visible peripheral objects before dense
   textures, stitches or repeated ornaments. Keep all parts of a movable object in its
   hierarchy, so a parent edit moves its upholstery, trim, legs and attachments together.
4. Derive contact heights from supporting geometry and use explicit anchors or bind where
   appropriate. Check contact after rotation or resizing. World AABB contact is approximate:
   curved surfaces and overlapping components require geometric interpretation. Do not
   treat intended intersections within a constructed part as physical collision failures.
5. Before execution, audit all API preconditions below. After a successful render, identify
   the largest visible disagreement and revise one main parameter family at a time. Check
   unrelated landmarks and support relations after the change. Preserve successful geometry
   during error repair. Missing render output is a failure, not visual evidence.
6. For an apparently missing object, check construction, unique inclusion keys, hierarchy,
   camera framing and intervening surfaces before adding a duplicate or enlarging it.
   Presence in a graph does not prove visibility. Absence from a truncated report does not
   prove omission. Do not infer whole-object scale from a probe on a decorative subpart.

Implementation checks grounded in the fixed API:
- All primitive dimensions and radii must be finite and positive. fillet_box requires
  0 < radius <= min(size)/2. For a thin object needing broad planar rounding, compose
  suitable primitives rather than increasing the fillet radius past this limit.
- Rod endpoints must differ; consecutive sweep_tube points must differ.
- include replaces an existing sibling with the same key. Use unique indexed keys in loops.
  It returns the attached node, which can be a clone; retain that returned reference.
- Layout functions and snap return copies. Attach the returned copy before binding it.
- Bind endpoints must already belong to the scene, cannot be ancestor/descendant, and
  dependencies must be acyclic. Supply source_anchor and target_anchor explicitly.
- realize clears Blender. Set camera, lights and bpy materials afterward. If customizing
  the world, first create and assign bpy.data.worlds.new('World') when scene.world is None,
  then enable use_nodes before accessing shader nodes.
- Semantic inclusion keys name Blender EMPTY markers; primitive mesh children may retain
  names such as Box or Rod. Apply material edits through the semantic group's descendants,
  not a presumed mesh name. Copy shared materials before object-specific modifications.
- Keep construction bounded. Procedural material patterns can represent fine surface detail
  without thousands of separate meshes. Do not change the runner's resource limits.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
The snap and bind calls above explicitly request bottom-to-top placement; their actual
source_anchor defaults are 'center', so do not omit anchors when expressing support.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
import bpy, math, random
from mathutils import Vector
from sceneact import *

random.seed(12)
scene = Scene("French chaise room")

# Observations: ivory striped chaise, tall curved left end, green and gilt
# carved frame, four curved feet, loose pillow, green label, paneled wall,
# left curtain, dark parquet, and a cropped cane chair at lower left.
# Camera assumptions: elevated view from the front and foot of the chaise;
# absolute scale is arbitrary. Long furniture axis is world X.

cream = (.77, .72, .61)
wallcolor = (.69, .66, .57)
green = (.29, .35, .29)
gold = (.55, .47, .30)
fabriccolor = (.83, .77, .65)

room = scene.include("architecture", Asset("architecture"))
room.include("floor_base", box((12,12,.10), center=(0,0,-.07), color=(.15,.075,.035)))
room.include("back_wall", box((10,.16,4), center=(0,1.10,2), color=wallcolor))

def rail(asset, name, pts, radius, color):
    return asset.include(name, sweep_tube(points=pts, radius=radius, color=color))

def smooth(points, steps=8):
    p = [Vector(points[0])] + [Vector(q) for q in points] + [Vector(points[-1])]
    out = []
    for i in range(1,len(p)-2):
        a,b,c,d = p[i-1:i+3]
        for j in range(steps):
            t=j/steps
            v=.5*((2*b)+(-a+c)*t+(2*a-5*b+4*c-d)*t*t+(-a+3*b-3*c+d)*t*t*t)
            out.append(tuple(v))
    out.append(tuple(p[-2]))
    return out

# Architecture builder: layered, shallow wall mouldings and a right pilaster.
for i,(z,h,depth) in enumerate([(0.09,.14,.08),(.20,.045,.055),(1.91,.045,.055),(2.02,.06,.07),(2.15,.035,.05)]):
    room.include(f"horizontal_moulding_{i}", box((9,depth,h), center=(0,.985-depth/2,z), color=cream))
for k,(xl,xr) in enumerate([(-3,-1.55),(-1.48,1.72),(1.84,3.1)]):
    for j,inset in enumerate([0,.037]):
        xa,xb=xl+inset,xr-inset
        za,zb=.35+inset,1.79-inset
        y=.989-j*.012
        for n,pts in enumerate([
            [(xa,y,za),(xb,y,za)],[(xa,y,zb),(xb,y,zb)],
            [(xa,y,za),(xa,y,zb)],[(xb,y,za),(xb,y,zb)]
        ]):
            rail(room,f"panel_{k}_{j}_{n}",pts,.012 if j==0 else .006,cream)
for i,x in enumerate([-.97,.47]):
    room.include(f"wall_joint_{i}", box((.006,.008,2.8), center=(x,1.009,1.4), color=(.40,.37,.30)))
room.include("right_pilaster",box((.40,.43,3.4),center=(2.22,.91,1.7),color=(.76,.75,.67)))
for i,x in enumerate([2.07,2.35]):
    room.include(f"pilaster_trim_{i}",box((.018,.022,2.9),center=(x,.682,1.6),color=cream))

# Parquet builder: bounded herringbone mesh tiles with slight color variation.
floor = scene.include("parquet", Asset("parquet"))
L,W=.66,.132
ang=math.radians(45)
def rotxy(x,y):
    return (math.cos(ang)*x-math.sin(ang)*y, math.sin(ang)*x+math.cos(ang)*y)
for i in range(-8,9):
    for j in range(-17,18):
        ox=i*L-j*W
        oy=i*L+j*W
        for typ in range(2):
            if typ==0:
                x,y=ox+L/2,oy+W/2
                sx,sy=L-.006,W-.006
            else:
                x,y=ox+L+W/2,oy+L/2
                sx,sy=W-.006,L-.006
            X,Y=rotxy(x,y)
            if abs(X)>4.6 or abs(Y)>4.6:
                continue
            c=random.uniform(.78,1.22)
            p=box((sx,sy,.025),center=(X,Y,-.006),
                  color=(.215*c,.105*c,.049*c))
            p.turn("z",45,pivot=(X,Y,-.006))
            floor.include(f"plank_{i}_{j}_{typ}",p)

chaise=scene.include("chaise",Asset("chaise"))
# Frame builder: cushion support, sculpted apron, continuous gilt edging.
chaise.include("seat_support",fillet_box((2.49,1.00,.15),radius=.07,
               center=(.10,0,.585),color=green))

front=[]
for i in range(45):
    x=-1.11+2.48*i/44
    z=.505-.035*math.cos((x-.10)*math.pi/1.25)
    front.append((x,-.515,z))
rail(chaise,"front_apron_lower",smooth(front,2),.045,green)
rail(chaise,"front_apron_gold",[(x,y-.026,z-.025) for x,y,z in front],.009,gold)
rail(chaise,"front_top_edge",[(-1.12,-.515,.665),(1.25,-.515,.665),(1.38,-.42,.62)],.025,gold)
rail(chaise,"back_under_edge",[(-1.12,.49,.58),(1.24,.49,.58),(1.38,.38,.57)],.036,green)

for index,(x,y) in enumerate([(-.99,-.41),(-.99,.39),(1.22,-.39),(1.22,.39)]):
    side=1 if x>0 else -1
    pts=[(x,y,.60),(x+.035*side,y,.44),(x-.055*side,y-.018,.23),
         (x-.025*side,y-.04,.065),(x+.045*side,y-.055,.045)]
    rail(chaise,f"curved_leg_{index}",smooth(pts,7),.043,green)
    rail(chaise,f"leg_gilt_{index}",smooth([(a,b-.035,c) for a,b,c in pts],7),.007,gold)
    chaise.include(f"foot_{index}",ball(.048,center=pts[-1],color=green))

# End shell outline: high rear crest, scooped front arm, and bowed lower panel.
top_end=[(-1.16,-.51,1.16),(-1.23,-.30,1.37),(-1.24,.04,1.56),
         (-1.14,.32,1.62),(-.99,.49,1.52)]
bottom_end=[(-1.06,-.50,.61),(-1.17,-.25,.59),(-1.20,.04,.61),
            (-1.10,.32,.66),(-.98,.49,.73)]
rail(chaise,"end_crest",smooth(top_end,10),.035,green)
rail(chaise,"end_crest_gilt",smooth([(x-.022,y,z+.014) for x,y,z in top_end],10),.008,gold)
rail(chaise,"end_base",smooth(bottom_end,10),.035,green)
rail(chaise,"front_end_post",smooth([top_end[0],(-1.10,-.52,1.00),(-1.07,-.51,.79),bottom_end[0]],10),.033,green)
rail(chaise,"rear_end_post",smooth([top_end[-1],(-1.02,.5,1.20),bottom_end[-1]],10),.03,green)
backline=[(-.99,.49,1.52),(-.82,.50,1.38),(-.59,.50,1.24),
          (-.40,.50,1.22),(-.37,.49,1.02),(-.19,.48,.85)]
rail(chaise,"rear_swept_rail",smooth(backline,10),.033,green)
rail(chaise,"rear_rail_gilt",smooth([(x,y-.025,z+.012) for x,y,z in backline],10),.008,gold)

# Small, economical carved ornaments on the frame.
for i in range(7):
    x=.10+(i-3)*.037
    z=.49+.035*math.cos((i-3)*.8)
    chaise.include(f"apron_rosette_{i}",ball(.032,center=(x,-.552,z),color=gold))
for side in [-1,1]:
    pts=[]
    for i in range(30):
        t=i/29*math.pi*2
        r=.015+.055*i/29
        pts.append((.10+side*(.12+r*math.cos(t)),-.556,.505+r*.55*math.sin(t)))
    rail(chaise,f"apron_scroll_{side}",pts,.009,gold)
for i in range(6):
    y=.16+i*.047
    chaise.include(f"crest_leaf_{i}",ball(.024,center=(-1.23,y,1.605+ .02*math.sin(i)),color=gold))

# Peripheral furniture and curtains are included before textile detail.
curtains=scene.include("curtains",Asset("curtains"))
for i in range(12):
    x=-2.02+i*.037
    y=.48+.035*math.sin(i*1.7)
    curtains.include(f"ivory_fold_{i}",rod(.033,start=(x,y,.02),end=(x,y,3.3),
                       color=(.82+.035*math.sin(i),.78+.03*math.sin(i),.67+.025*math.sin(i))))
curtains.include("window_light",box((.5,.05,3.3),center=(-2.16,.72,1.65),color=(.94,.95,.89)))

chair=scene.include("foreground_cane_chair",Asset("foreground_cane_chair"))
chair.include("seat",fillet_box((.68,.65,.065),radius=.032,center=(-1.53,-1.43,.46),color=green))
for i,(a,b) in enumerate([
    ((-1.85,-1.75,.50),(-1.20,-1.75,.50)),
    ((-1.85,-1.12,.50),(-1.20,-1.12,.50)),
    ((-1.85,-1.75,.50),(-1.85,-1.12,.50)),
    ((-1.20,-1.75,.50),(-1.20,-1.12,.50))
]):
    rail(chair,f"seat_rim_{i}",[a,b],.026,gold)
for i in range(27):
    t=i*.021
    rail(chair,f"cane_x_{i}",[(-1.81,-1.71+t,.50),(-1.24,-1.71+t,.50)],.0045,(.54,.39,.21))
    rail(chair,f"cane_y_{i}",[(-1.81+t,-1.71,.502),(-1.81+t,-1.16,.502)],.0045,(.62,.48,.28))

realize(scene)

# Mesh upholstery is parented to the semantic chaise marker.
root=bpy.data.objects.get("chaise")
def material(name,color,roughness=.7):
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.diffuse_color=(*color,1)
    m.use_nodes=True
    bs=m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    bs.inputs["Base Color"].default_value=(*color,1)
    bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=roughness
    return m

upholstery=material("woven ivory with faded rose pinstripes",(.82,.76,.65))
n=upholstery.node_tree.nodes
l=upholstery.node_tree.links
bs=n.get("Principled BSDF")
tex=n.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
sep=n.new("ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ")
l.new(tex.outputs["Generated"],sep.inputs[0])
mult=n.new("ShaderNodeMath");mult.operation="MULTIPLY";mult.inputs[1].default_value=105
l.new(sep.outputs["Y"],mult.inputs[0])
sine=n.new("ShaderNodeMath");sine.operation="SINE";l.new(mult.outputs[0],sine.inputs[0])
threshold=n.new("ShaderNodeMath");threshold.operation="GREATER_THAN";threshold.inputs[1].default_value=.975
l.new(sine.outputs[0],threshold.inputs[0])
noise=n.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise");noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value=145
noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value=2
l.new(tex.outputs["Generated"],noise.inputs["Vector"])
mix=n.new("ShaderNodeMixRGB")
mix.inputs[1].default_value=(.84,.79,.69,1)
mix.inputs[2].default_value=(.53,.31,.29,1)
l.new(threshold.outputs[0],mix.inputs[0])
l.new(mix.outputs[0],bs.inputs["Base Color"])
bump=n.new("ShaderNodeBump");bump.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.17;bump.inputs["Distance"].default_value=.009
l.new(noise.outputs["Fac"],bump.inputs["Height"]);l.new(bump.outputs[0],bs.inputs["Normal"])

pillowmat=material("pillow warm ivory",(.82,.76,.63))
pn=pillowmat.node_tree.nodes;pl=pillowmat.node_tree.links
noise2=pn.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise");noise2.inputs["Scale"].default_value=110
bump2=pn.new("ShaderNodeBump");bump2.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.22;bump2.inputs["Distance"].default_value=.012
pl.new(noise2.outputs["Fac"],bump2.inputs["Height"])
pl.new(bump2.outputs[0],pn.get("Principled BSDF").inputs["Normal"])

def mesh_obj(name,verts,faces,mat,parent=root):
    mesh=bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    mesh.from_pydata(verts,[],faces);mesh.update()
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,mesh);bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.data.materials.append(mat)
    if parent:ob.parent=parent
    for p in mesh.polygons:p.use_smooth=True
    return ob

def spow(a,p):
    return math.copysign(abs(a)**p,a)

def softbox(name,center,radii,mat,exponents=(.34,.45),rotation=(0,0,0)):
    verts=[];faces=[]
    nu,nv=96,40
    for j in range(nv+1):
        v=-math.pi/2+math.pi*j/nv
        for i in range(nu):
            u=2*math.pi*i/nu
            cv=spow(math.cos(v),exponents[1])
            verts.append((radii[0]*spow(math.cos(u),exponents[0])*cv,
                          radii[1]*spow(math.sin(u),exponents[0])*cv,
                          radii[2]*spow(math.sin(v),exponents[1])))
    for j in range(nv):
        for i in range(nu):
            a=j*nu+i;b=j*nu+(i+1)%nu
            faces.append((a,b,b+nu,a+nu))
    ob=mesh_obj(name,verts,faces,mat)
    ob.location=center
    ob.rotation_euler=tuple(math.radians(v) for v in rotation)
    return ob

softbox("long upholstered mattress",(.12,0,.735),(1.28,.515,.155),upholstery,(.32,.50))
# End upholstery surface between the bowed base and crest.
top=smooth(top_end,12);bot=smooth(bottom_end,12)
verts=[];faces=[]
for j in range(17):
    t=j/16
    for i in range(len(top)):
        a=Vector(bot[i]);b=Vector(top[i])
        q=a.lerp(b,t)
        q.x-=.035*math.sin(math.pi*t)
        verts.append(tuple(q))
for j in range(16):
    for i in range(len(top)-1):
        a=j*len(top)+i
        faces.append((a,a+1,a+1+len(top),a+len(top)))
ob=mesh_obj("upholstered curved head end",verts,faces,upholstery)
solid=ob.modifiers.new("padded shell thickness","SOLIDIFY");solid.thickness=.045
bev=ob.modifiers.new("soft upholstery edges","BEVEL");bev.width=.025;bev.segments=3

# Low upholstered wing beneath the curved far-side frame.
line=smooth(backline,10)
verts=[];faces=[]
for i,p in enumerate(line):
    verts.extend([(p[0],p[1],.77),(p[0],p[1],p[2]-.025)])
for i in range(len(line)-1):
    faces.append((2*i,2*i+2,2*i+3,2*i+1))
ob=mesh_obj("rear upholstered wing",verts,faces,upholstery)
sol=ob.modifiers.new("wing thickness","SOLIDIFY");sol.thickness=.05
softbox("loose square ivory pillow",(-.77,-.055,1.15),(.14,.345,.355),
        pillowmat,(.35,.45),(0,-18,-7))

# Narrow piping follows the seat perimeter.
def curve_obj(name,pts,radius,mat):
    cu=bpy.data.curves.new(name,"CURVE");cu.dimensions="3D"
    sp=cu.splines.new("POLY");sp.points.add(len(pts)-1)
    for p,q in zip(sp.points,pts):p.co=(*q,1)
    cu.bevel_depth=radius;cu.bevel_resolution=2
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,cu);bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.data.materials.append(mat);ob.parent=root
    return ob
pipingmat=material("ivory piping",(.69,.60,.44))
pts=[]
for i in range(161):
    a=i/160*math.tau
    pts.append((.12+1.28*spow(math.cos(a),.32),.515*spow(math.sin(a),.32),.72))
curve_obj("mattress welt",pts,.008,pipingmat)

# Small green museum label on the top of the seat.
labelmat=material("dark green label",(.055,.20,.16))
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1,location=(.67,.12,.899))
label=bpy.context.object;label.name="green museum label"
label.dimensions=(.085,.23,.004);label.rotation_euler[2]=math.radians(-7)
label.data.materials.append(labelmat);label.parent=root
letter=material("label lettering",(.69,.76,.63))
for i in range(3):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1,location=(.671,.15+i*.019,.903))
    o=bpy.context.object;o.name=f"label lettering {i}"
    o.dimensions=(.039 if i==0 else .026,.004,.001)
    o.data.materials.append(letter);o.parent=root

# Gentle wood grain on the parquet, preserving the individual plank colors.
for ob in bpy.data.objects:
    if ob.type=="MESH" and ob.parent and "parquet" in ob.parent.name.lower():
        for old in ob.data.materials:
            old.use_nodes=True
            ns=old.node_tree.nodes;ls=old.node_tree.links
            b=ns.get("Principled BSDF")
```
